title: Sentiment Analysis End‑to‑End 🎭
description: Build a complete pipeline: preprocess movie reviews, embed, train an LSTM, and predict sentiment with >85% accuracy.

slides.title: Putting It All Together 🧩
slides.content:
# Sentiment Analysis on IMDB Reviews

We'll build a model that classifies movie reviews as positive or negative.

Dataset: IMDB dataset (50k reviews, balanced), built into Keras.

Pipeline:
1. Load data and inspect.
2. Preprocess: tokenize, pad sequences.
3. Build an Embedding + LSTM model.
4. Train and evaluate.

We aim for >85% validation accuracy.

slides.title: Load & Preprocess 🐍
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.datasets import imdb
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.sequence import pad_sequences

max_features = 10000  # vocabulary size
max_len = 500  # max words per review

(X_train, y_train), (X_test, y_test) = imdb.load_data(num_words=max_features)
X_train = pad_sequences(X_train, maxlen=max_len)
X_test = pad_sequences(X_test, maxlen=max_len)

slides.title: Model Architecture 🏗️
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.models import Sequential
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Embedding, LSTM, Dense, Dropout

model = Sequential([
    Embedding(max_features, 128, input_length=max_len),
    LSTM(64, dropout=0.2, recurrent_dropout=0.2),
    Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.summary()

quizData.question: Why do we use `pad_sequences` after loading IMDB?

options.text: To ensure all input sequences have the same length (required for batch processing in neural networks)

quizData.explanation: Neural networks expect fixed‑size inputs; padding truncates or zero‑pads sequences to `max_len`.

slides.title: Train & Evaluate 🏋️
slides.codeSnippet:
history = model.fit(X_train, y_train, batch_size=64, epochs=5,
                    validation_split=0.2)

test_loss, test_acc = model.evaluate(X_test, y_test)
print(f"Test accuracy: {test_acc:.3f}")

slides.title: Results & Improvement 📈
slides.content:
# Expected Performance

With this simple LSTM, you should reach ~87‑88% validation accuracy in 5 epochs.

To improve further:
- Use pre‑trained word embeddings (GloVe) in the Embedding layer.
- Add Bidirectional LSTM.
- Add convolutional layers (1D Conv) before LSTM for n‑gram features.
- Increase `max_features` or `max_len`.
- Use BERT/RoBERTa (transformer‑based) for state‑of‑the‑art.

This project demonstrates the entire NLP pipeline from raw text to classification.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Transfer Learning in NLP
Just like ImageNet for vision, there are pre‑trained language models (BERT, GPT) that you can fine‑tune on your task. They dominate modern NLP. Explore Hugging Face `transformers` library.
